questions.question: In 2026, which country will host Asian Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Japan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Japan** will host the 2026 Asian Games.
 
• The Asian Games, also known as Asiad, is a continental multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from all over Asia.
 
• The event is regulated by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA).
 
• Japan has previously hosted the Asian Games in 1958 and 1994.
 
• The 2026 Asian Games will be held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Olympic Council of Asia (OCA)** is the governing body of sports in Asia, responsible for organizing the Asian Games.
 
• The first Asian Games were held in **1951** in New Delhi, India.
 
• The Asian Games feature a wide range of sports, including both Olympic sports and sports unique to Asia.
 
• Japan is known for its strong infrastructure and experience in hosting international sporting events.
 
• The selection of Japan as the host for the 2026 Asian Games was announced in **2016**.

questions.question: Who is Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission as on 31 March 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shri Manoj Soni**__

__
 
• **Shri Manoj Soni** is the Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) as of 31 March 2024.
 
• The Union Public Service Commission is India's premier central recruiting agency responsible for appointments to and examinations for All India services and group A & group B of Central services.
 
• UPSC conducts various exams including the Civil Services Examination (CSE), Engineering Services Examination (ESE), Combined Defence Services Examination (CDSE), and others.
 
• The Chairman and other members of the UPSC are appointed by the President of India.
 
• Shri Manoj Soni has a distinguished academic and administrative career, having previously served as the Vice-Chancellor of Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Open University and The Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UPSC** was established on 1 October 1926 as Public Service Commission and later reconstituted as Federal Public Service Commission by the Government of India Act, 1935; it was later renamed as Union Public Service Commission after independence.
 
• The Commission is headquartered at Dholpur House, in New Delhi.
 
• UPSC is among the few institutions which function with both autonomy and freedom, along with the country's higher judiciary and lately the Election Commission.
 
• UPSC's mandate is to conduct examinations for recruitment to various services of the Union and to advise the President on disciplinary matters.

questions.question: Who is the author of the Indian national anthem?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rabindranath Tagore**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore** is the author of the Indian national anthem, "Jana Gana Mana".
 
• The anthem was originally composed in Bengali and was later translated into Hindi.
 
• Rabindranath Tagore was a renowned poet, writer, and the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.
 
• "Jana Gana Mana" was adopted as the national anthem of India on January 24, 1950.
 
• The anthem reflects the unity and diversity of India, embodying the country's rich cultural heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rabindranath Tagore** was born on May 7, 1861, in Calcutta (now Kolkata), India.
 
• He was a polymath who contributed to various fields such as literature, music, and art.
 
• Tagore founded the Visva-Bharati University in Santiniketan, which remains a prominent educational institution.
 
• He was also known for his role in the Indian independence movement, although he was more of a cultural and spiritual leader than a political one.
 
• Tagore's works include the famous collection of poems "Gitanjali" for which he received the Nobel Prize.
 
• In addition to "Jana Gana Mana", he also composed the national anthem of Bangladesh, "Amar Shonar Bangla".

questions.question: The process of merging data from a data source into a main document in a word - processing application is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**mail merge**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mail merge** is a process in word-processing applications that involves merging data from a data source into a main document.
 
• This technique is commonly used for generating personalized letters, labels, and envelopes.
 
• During a mail merge, placeholders in the main document are replaced with data from the data source.
 
• Applications like Microsoft Word often have built-in features to facilitate mail merge operations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Data sources** for mail merge can include databases, spreadsheets, or other structured data files.
 
• The main document typically contains static text and placeholders for dynamic data.
 
• Mail merge is particularly useful for businesses and organizations that need to send bulk communications.
 
• It helps in automating the process of creating personalized documents, saving time and reducing errors.

questions.question: Which MS Excel function can be used to sum up the numbers entered in a group of cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SUM**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **SUM** function in MS Excel is used to add up the numbers in a range of cells.
 
• The **SUM** function is written as =SUM(range), where range is the group of cells you want to sum up.
 
• This function can handle both individual cell references and ranges, making it versatile for various summing tasks.
 
• Using the **SUM** function simplifies the process of adding numbers, as opposed to manually entering each value.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other functions like **AVERAGE**, **MAX**, and **COUNT** serve different purposes:

 
 
• **AVERAGE**: Calculates the average of a group of numbers.
 
• **MAX**: Finds the maximum value in a range of cells.
 
• **COUNT**: Counts the number of cells that contain numbers.
 
 
 
• To use the **SUM** function, you can type =SUM(A1:A10) in a cell to sum the values from cell A1 to A10.
 
• The **SUM** function is part of the basic mathematical functions available in Excel, making it essential for data analysis and financial calculations.

questions.question: In 1960, which isotope was used to define the standard measure of length?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krypton-86**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Krypton-86** was used in 1960 to define the standard measure of length.
 
• The length of the meter was defined based on the wavelength of the radiation emitted by Krypton-86.
 
• This definition was adopted by the 11th General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM) in 1960.
 
• It was later replaced in 1983 by the definition based on the speed of light.
 
• The use of Krypton-86 provided a more precise and reproducible standard compared to the previous definitions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM)** is the international authority responsible for uniformity in measurements.
 
• In 1983, the meter was redefined as the distance light travels in a vacuum in 1/299,792,458 seconds.
 
• This new definition ties the unit of length directly to a fundamental constant of nature, the speed of light.
 
• The redefinition aimed to increase the precision and universality of the meter as a unit of measure.

questions.question: The music of traditional _______ consists of thumri and other lyrical song forms.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The music of traditional **Kathak** consists of thumri and other lyrical song forms.
 
• **Kathak** is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.
 
• It traces its origins to the nomadic bards of ancient northern India, known as **Kathakars** or storytellers.
 
• The name **Kathak** is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Katha' meaning story, and 'Kathakar' meaning the one who tells a story.
 
• Traditional Kathak dance often includes music that is rich in thumri, which is a semi-classical vocal form of North India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathak** dance form has three main gharanas (schools) - Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras.
 
• Each gharana has its own unique features and emphasis on different aspects of the dance form.
 
• The Lucknow gharana, for instance, places a strong emphasis on the expressiveness of the dance, while the Jaipur gharana is known for its intricate footwork.
 
• The dance form has evolved over time and has been influenced by both Hindu and Muslim cultures, especially during the Mughal era.
 
• Kathak performances often include stories from Indian epics like Mahabharata and Ramayana.

questions.question: Which directive principle has been implemented in establishing Handloom and Handicrafts Boards?

options.text: Promote cottage industries on cooperative basis
Participation of workers in management of Industries
Provision for just and humane condition of work

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Promote cottage industries on cooperative basis**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Promote cottage industries on cooperative basis** is a directive principle implemented in establishing Handloom and Handicrafts Boards.
 
• Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government. These are provided in Part IV of the Constitution of India.
 
• The aim of these principles is to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They act as a yardstick in the hands of the people to measure the performance of the government.
 
• Promotion of cottage industries on a cooperative basis helps in the economic development of rural areas and provides employment opportunities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy** are borrowed from the Irish Constitution and aim to promote social and economic democracy.
 
• They are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
• However, they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country, and it is the duty of the state to apply these principles in making laws.
 
• Some other important directive principles include the provision for adequate means of livelihood, equal pay for equal work, protection of childhood and youth, and organization of village panchayats.

questions.question: Which of the following planets’ atmosphere is made up of thick white and yellowish clouds of sulphuric acid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Venus**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Venus** has a very thick atmosphere composed mainly of carbon dioxide, with clouds of sulfuric acid, making it the hottest planet in the Solar System.
 
• The atmosphere is so dense that it creates a runaway greenhouse effect, trapping heat and raising surface temperatures to around 465 degrees Celsius (869 degrees Fahrenheit).
 
• The thick clouds of sulfuric acid reflect sunlight, giving Venus its characteristic yellowish-white appearance when observed from space.
 
• The atmospheric pressure on Venus is approximately 92 times greater than Earth's, which is equivalent to the pressure found 900 meters (3,000 feet) underwater on Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Venus** is the second planet from the Sun and is similar in size and structure to Earth, earning it the nickname "Earth's twin."
 
• Despite its similarities to Earth, the conditions on Venus are extremely harsh and inhospitable.
 
• The planet rotates very slowly on its axis and in the opposite direction to most planets in the Solar System, including Earth.
 
• Venus has been explored by various spacecraft, including NASA's Magellan mission, which mapped the planet's surface using radar.
 
• Due to its thick cloud cover, the surface of Venus cannot be observed directly from space in visible light.

questions.question: Which is the Standard Meridian of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**82º30ʹ E**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Standard Meridian of India** is **82º30ʹ E**.
 
• This meridian passes through **Mirzapur** in Uttar Pradesh and is the reference for Indian Standard Time (IST).
 
• Indian Standard Time is 5 hours and 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT+5:30).
 
• The selection of this meridian helps in maintaining a uniform time across India, despite its vast longitudinal extent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India spans approximately **30 degrees of longitude**, from 68º7ʹ E to 97º25ʹ E.
 
• The concept of a standard meridian helps in avoiding confusion caused by having multiple local times.
 
• The decision to adopt 82º30ʹ E as the Standard Meridian was made during the era of British India to ensure uniformity in timekeeping across the country.
 
• Before this standardization, different regions followed their own local time, leading to inconsistencies.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a monopoly?

options.text: Full control over the price by the seller

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One buyer and many sellers**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A monopoly is characterized by **one seller and many buyers**.
 
• In a monopoly, there are **no close substitutes** for the product or service provided by the seller.
 
• The seller in a monopoly has **full control over the price** of the product or service.
 
• The market condition of **one buyer and many sellers** describes a monopsony, not a monopoly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **monopoly** exists when a specific person or enterprise is the only supplier of a particular commodity.
 
• This contrasts with a **monopsony** where there is only one buyer and many sellers.
 
• Monopolies can be established by a government, form naturally over time, or form as a conglomerate of companies.
 
• Monopolies can lead to **higher prices and inferior products** due to the lack of competition.
 
• Antitrust laws in many countries regulate monopolistic practices to protect consumers.

questions.question: The Constitution of India was adopted on ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sat Nov 26 1949 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.
 
• While the Constitution was adopted on 26th November 1949, it **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **97 topics** are currently listed in India's Union List.
 
• The Union List is one of the **three lists** in the **Seventh Schedule** to the Constitution of India, granting powers to the Union government to legislate on these topics.
 
• Subjects under the **Union List include defense, foreign affairs, railways, banking, among others,** where the central government has exclusive powers to legislate.
 
• The list reflects the subjects that are of national importance and require uniformity of legislation across the country.

questions.question: Due to the efforts of whom among the following social reformers was the first Hindu Widow Remarriage Act introduced and passed in 1856?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar** was instrumental in the introduction and passage of the first Hindu Widow Remarriage Act in 1856.
 
• He was a prominent social reformer and educator in India, advocating for various social changes including the upliftment of women and education for all.
 
• The Hindu Widow Remarriage Act, 1856, legally permitted the remarriage of Hindu widows, which was a significant step towards improving the social status of women in India.
 
• Vidyasagar's efforts were crucial in challenging orthodox Hindu practices and promoting progressive reforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar** was born on 26 September 1820 in Birsingha, Bengal Presidency, British India.
 
• He was a key figure in the Bengal Renaissance and worked tirelessly for the education and rights of women.
 
• Vidyasagar's contributions were not limited to widow remarriage; he also worked on promoting education, especially for girls, and improving the Bengali prose.
 
• His efforts laid the foundation for many subsequent social reforms in India.

questions.question: Give Plastic and Take Gold scheme was launched in the village of which State/UT in year 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jammu and Kashmir**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Give Plastic and Take Gold scheme** was launched in the village of **Jammu and Kashmir** in the year 2023.
 
• This innovative scheme aims to encourage the collection of plastic waste by offering gold as an incentive.
 
• The initiative is part of a broader effort to promote environmental sustainability and reduce plastic pollution in the region.
 
• Under this scheme, villagers can exchange a certain amount of collected plastic for a specified amount of gold, thus motivating them to participate actively in the cleanup drive.
 
• The scheme is expected to have a significant positive impact on the local environment and set an example for other regions to follow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jammu and Kashmir** has been at the forefront of various environmental initiatives aimed at preserving its natural beauty and resources.
 
• The region is known for its picturesque landscapes, which are often threatened by pollution and waste.
 
• Government and local bodies have been increasingly focusing on sustainable development and environmental conservation.
 
• Such innovative schemes not only help in waste management but also raise awareness among the community about the importance of environmental protection.
 
• This scheme aligns with the broader national goals of reducing plastic waste and promoting sustainable practices across India.
